sections.title: In brief
sections.text: Knight extends grammar-based comparison from whole styles to individual designs.

sections.title: Question or aim
sections.text: How can two designs be compared through their constructive organization?

sections.title: Approach described
sections.text: Represent each design as a decomposition into shapes and spatial relations; align comparable elements and trace shape-by-shape transformations.

sections.title: What the abstract supports
sections.text: The abstract reports a framework for exposing design relationships and proposes a simple similarity measure.

sections.title: What remains unverified
sections.text: Only the publisher-deposited Crossref abstract was read. The exact similarity formula, worked cases and qualifications require the complete article; no perceptual validation or statistical performance is established here.

sections.title: Why it may help
sections.text: It suggests comparing how designs are assembled, alongside comparing their visible outlines.
